covers: the two value domains accept only cash/credit and goods/expense, treat None as 'leave it alone', and tell the user-facing entry (which refuses an empty string) from the internal correction route (which may write one)

checks.note: the master-data family's pure modules together

covers: a supplier profile saved in two parts: the field that was given changes, the one left out keeps its value, and the anchor comes back cleaned
the user entry refuses an empty value, an unknown value and a malformed tax id, and writes nothing
a learned correction cannot overwrite a user rule (and can still fill a tax id it owns)
removing a profile clears its effect, keeps the auditable row, and is an idempotent no-op afterwards (unknown tax id and blank tax id included)
supplier profiles follow the feature, the role (read-only may list, may not write) and the company
the import preview reports valid/error/error/valid/skip and writes nothing
the import commit creates, skips the duplicate inside the same batch, maps phone to contact_phone, and re-running it lands every existing row in skip
a duplicate tax id is refused by the single create and by the update (exclude-self still allowed), and clearing a tax id stays allowed
import permissions follow the feature and the company

checks.note: the terminology table is self-consistent; it does not prove the new service-layer strings have translations (recorded as a cross-batch glossary debt)

intentional_differences: removing a supplier profile clears its two defaults and keeps the auditable native row (the deployed delete dropped the row): native push inputs are auditable and refuse on_trash, and the read side ends up identical because a row with no effect leaves the profile list and the push verdict without a profile
the profile list does not carry supplier_name: the deployed read-side enrichment joins the purchase domain's suppliers master, which this repository does not have

tax-id uniqueness compares digit-normalised values on both sides (the deployed check compared the stored string): the thirteen digits are the client's identity for buyer matching and ERP reconciliation, so the same number written differently must not create a second client. This also applies to the single create and update, as it did in the deployed subject create/update
the import rows map phone to the native contact_phone, branch/address/tax_id keep their names
the import parse endpoint (xlsx/csv to headers and rows) is still not ported: parsing is a device, and the endpoint only takes rows
the deployed preview reports a duplicate inside the same batch as valid (the first row is not in the database yet) and the commit lands it in skip: the native preview keeps that behaviour
comments and docstrings were rewritten; every value domain, the thirteen-digit rule, the partial-update semantics, the source precedence and the three import error codes are the deployed ones
not_run: the supplier master (the deployed read-side name enrichment has no native source yet), duplicate-invoice detection, the expense category tree and the supplier-to-category memory, the M1 Thai-name gate (all four have an attribution conclusion and await a product decision), the frontend, deployment, push, merge and user acceptance
